The reminder fired because the staging check mistook the letters in your commit message for the `-a` flag. That's fixed and committed as `a209ddd`.

**Cause (verified):** `shlex.split` turns `git commit -m"add export handler"` into the single word `-madd export handler`. The old scan looked at every letter in a short-option cluster, so the `a` in "add" matched `commit -a`. Your message text was being read as flags.

**Fix (verified):** In `src/staging.py`, a cluster now stops at the first letter that takes a value (`m`, `F`, `c`, `C`, `t`, `u`, `S` for commit). Everything after that letter is the value, not flags. `git commit -am "x"` still counts as staging everything.

**Regression test (verified):** I added `test_message_text_with_stage_letters_is_not_a_stage_flag` to `tests/test_staging.py` before changing the code. It failed on all three cases, then passed after the fix. The full suite runs 6 tests, all passing. I also checked a few edge cases, such as `-ma`, `-aF msg`, `-fA`, and `-- -A`, and they behave correctly.

**Not verified:** I didn't find where the reminder is wired into your tooling. The repo has no active git hooks. I'm inferring that the reminder calls `stages_all`, which is the only staging logic in the repo.

**Left alone:** The uncommitted `README.md` note ("ask whether Export should include cancelled orders") and the untracked `notes/` folder are not part of this fix, so I didn't commit them.
